curriculum.sourceReference: Topic scope aligned to the Class 6 Mathematics fractions syllabus; all content original.

chapter.title: Patterns in Mathematics
chapter.summary: Mathematics is the study of patterns. Here students learn to find the repeating part of a pattern, to describe a number sequence by its rule, and to count how a shape pattern grows. The habit to build: look closely, say the rule in words, then test it on every step.
keyIdeas: Find the repeating unit before you predict.
A rule must work for every step, not just the first two.
Say the rule in words before using numbers.

provenance.note: Authored by the Adhyaapak team; topic scope follows the Class 6 Mathematics syllabus. Recommend review by a subject teacher.

concepts.title: Spotting repeating patterns
concepts.description: A pattern repeats in a predictable way. The repeating part is called the unit.
concepts.learningObjective: Find the repeating unit of a pattern and use it to say what comes next.
concepts.teacherNote: Use classroom objects first (claps, colours, seating). Ask 'what stays the same?' before 'what comes next?'.

content.summary: A pattern is something that repeats in a way we can predict. The part that repeats is the unit.
steps: Look at the pattern: A B B A B B A B B.
Find where it starts to repeat. The unit is A B B.
To continue the pattern, keep repeating A B B.

content.summary: Use the length of the unit to jump far along a pattern without writing it all out.

workedExample.problem: In A B B A B B A B B …, what is the 10th item?
steps: The unit A B B has 3 items.
A remainder of 1 means the 1st item of the unit.

content.commonError: Looking only at the last few items instead of finding the whole repeating unit.

content.summary: Use the unit to answer questions about positions and counts.
content.prompt: A necklace repeats red, red, blue, green. What colour is bead 25? How many blue beads are there in the first 40 beads?

concepts.title: Number sequences and their rules
concepts.description: A number sequence follows a rule such as 'add 3' or 'double'.
concepts.learningObjective: Find the rule of a number sequence and use it to extend the sequence.
concepts.teacherNote: Ask students to say the rule aloud in words. Many can continue a sequence but cannot describe the rule.

content.summary: To find the rule, look at how each number changes to get the next one.
steps: The same change each time means the rule is 'add 3'.

content.summary: Check the rule on every step before you trust it.

workedExample.problem: Find the rule and the next two numbers: 100, 90, 80, 70.
steps: Each number is 10 less than the one before.
The next two numbers are 60 and 50.

content.commonError: Checking only the first two numbers. Test the rule on every step.

content.prompt: A sequence starts at 3 and each number is double the one before: 3, 6, 12, … What is the 6th number? Is it more than 100?

concepts.title: Growing shape patterns
concepts.description: In a growing pattern, each figure uses more pieces than the one before.
concepts.learningObjective: Count how a shape pattern grows and use the growth to find the number of pieces in a later figure.
concepts.teacherNote: Let students build the first three figures with sticks or counters. The 'shared stick' idea is the usual stumbling block.

content.summary: Count the sticks in each figure to see how many are added each time.
steps: Two triangles side by side use 5 sticks.

content.summary: Turn what you notice into a rule, then test it.

workedExample.problem: How many sticks are needed for 10 triangles in a row?
steps: Each triangle adds 2 sticks, and there is 1 extra stick at the start.

content.commonError: Multiplying by 3 because one triangle has 3 sticks. Triangles share sticks, and a shared stick is counted once.

content.summary: Find the rule for a new shape on your own.
content.prompt: Squares in a row use 4 sticks for the first square and 3 more for each new square. How many sticks for 12 squares? Which figure uses 40 sticks?

questions.explanation: The numbers go up by 2 each time, so the next number is 8 + 2 = 10.

questions.stem: The pattern A B B A B B A B B repeats. What is the 10th letter?
questions.explanation: The unit A B B has 3 letters. 10 ÷ 3 leaves 1, so the 10th letter is the 1st letter of the unit: A.

questions.stem: In the pattern ● ▲ ■ ● ▲ ■ ● ▲ ■ …, which shape is 7th?
questions.explanation: The unit has 3 shapes. 7 ÷ 3 leaves 1, so the 7th shape is the 1st of the unit: ●.
Each number is half of the one before, so the next is 8 ÷ 2 = 4.

questions.stem: Which sequence follows the rule 'start at 4, add 6'?
Triangles in a row use 3, 5, 7, … sticks. How many sticks for 4 triangles?
A row of n triangles uses 2n + 1 sticks. How many sticks for 8 triangles?
Squares in a row use 4, 7, 10, 13 sticks. How many sticks are added with each new square?
